title: Moral Self-correction is Not An Innate Capability in Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using the BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA) dataset via multiple-choice question answering on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on gender stereotypes, as well as a self-distinguishing task requiring the model to explicitly identify the stereotyped gender group.

Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice question answering on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on racial/ethnic stereotypes, as well as a self-distinguishing task requiring the model to identify the stereotyped racial group.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice QA on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on socioeconomic status (SES) stereotypes, alongside a self-distinguishing task.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice QA on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on stereotypes regarding physical appearance, alongside a self-distinguishing task.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice QA on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on disability status stereotypes, alongside a self-distinguishing task.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice QA on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on religious stereotypes, alongside a self-distinguishing task.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice QA on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on nationality-based stereotypes, alongside a self-distinguishing task.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice QA on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on sexual orientation stereotypes, alongside a self-distinguishing task.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark via multiple-choice QA on ambiguous contexts to measure reliance on age-related stereotypes, alongside a self-distinguishing task.

Evaluated using the RealToxicity benchmark by measuring the toxicity scores of generated text completions, alongside a self-distinguishing simulation task where models must select the less toxic response between two generated options.
